{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjccM8AAAABftDDcA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3IfzhJLNhM", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3If", "number": 97, "title": "Add optional retro LCD display shaders with pixel grid, ghosting, and model presets", "body": "## Problem

The player currently renders the Rust/Wasm core's **224×144 RGBA framebuffer** as crisp nearest-neighbor pixels using a **2D Canvas**. This is accurate for debugging, but visually much cleaner than a handheld WonderSwan LCD feels: there is no visible pixel-cell structure, mild liquid-crystal blur, display persistence/ghosting or panel-specific presentation.

The request is to make the web player feel more like a **period handheld LCD**, **not a CRT monitor**, while preserving the ability to choose the current clean output. This must be a **presentation-only, reversible effect**, not a change to the emulated display registers, timing, game pixels, input or save data.

## Expected outcome

A player can switch the display treatment live, without restarting the cartridge, through a compact, accessible setting:

- **Clean:** the existing sharp, pixel-exact nearest-neighbor presentation, useful for readability and pixel-level debugging.
- **LCD Light:** a subtle per-pixel LCD grid/matrix, slight pixel-cell shaping/softening and very mild persistence. This is the preferred *new-visitor default* if WebGL is available; keep text/menus comfortably readable.
- **LCD Authentic:** a stronger—but still usable—LCD-style matrix, restrained softness/ghosting and **model-aware** panel color/contrast and response presets. “Authentic” names a design aesthetic, **not** a claim of calibrated physical LCD measurements.
- **Retro CRT:** a separate, clearly labeled optional stylized mode with very subtle scanlines/mask; explicitly **not** the historically correct WonderSwan panel. It can be implemented as a small variant of the same shader pipeline, without a separate engine or elaborate CRT geometry.

Effects must be visually distinguishable from Clean and one another using an original CC0 game or synthetic framebuffer, but not exaggerate blur, scanlines or persistence at the expense of playability. A player can always switch to Clean immediately.

## Context and reproduction

Current `main` implementation:

- [`web/src/main.ts`](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/web/src/main.ts) obtains `canvas.getContext("2d")`, calls `putImageData(new ImageData(machine.framebuffer(), 224, 144))` in `draw()`, and uses `requestAnimationFrame` only while emulation is running. `sizeScreen()` handles pixel-aligned scaling and delegates portrait presentation to CSS. This is the **presentation integration point**.
- [`web/src/style.css`](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/web/src/style.css) applies `image-rendering: pixelated` and `rotate(-90deg)` in portrait mode; the view can be responsive, full-screen, or 144×224 portrait.
- [`web/index.html`](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/web/index.html) keeps the game-first UI compact and places secondary settings in the existing **Settings / Help** dialog.
- The Rust core (e.g. [`crates/ws-core/src/video.rs`](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/crates/ws-core/src/video.rs)) already emulates pixel content and parts of the LCD line pipeline. Those core computations must remain untouched. CSS-only opacity overlays must not be mistaken for emulation or for a faithful pixel-matrix shader.
- [README UI/UX principles](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/README.md#uiux): **Keep it simple; Show, don't tell; Intuitive and predictable.** Follow [development flow](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md), [review guidelines](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/docs/review-guidelines.md), [Issue template](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/issue.md) and [test/CI performance guidance](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md#test-and-ci-performance-principles).
- Existing production-preview Playwright checks in `web/scripts/smoke.mjs`, `web/scripts/compat.mjs`, `web/scripts/keypad.mjs` and `web/scripts/lcd-output.mjs` assert real player visuals/pixels and must not be broken. Existing exact-pixel checks may explicitly select **Clean** rather than weakening visual assertions.

### Rendering requirements

1. **Independent presentation stage:** Consume the original RGBA framebuffer without modifying its bytes or Rust/Wasm API. Prefer a minimal **WebGL2 fragment-shader post-processing** path that uploads the 224×144 image with nearest-neighbor sampling. Keep a reliable **existing-style 2D Clean fallback** when WebGL is unavailable, initialization fails, or context is lost. A dedicated output canvas or equivalent clean architecture is necessary because a canvas with an established 2D context cannot also use WebGL2. Avoid new rendering frameworks/dependencies.
2. **Pixel grid / pixel-cell appearance:** Compute the grid from **native emulated pixel coordinates**, not from CSS viewport pixels. Delineate pixels delicately using a controllable inset, luminance/edge falloff or matrix-cell shaping. Avoid arbitrary RGB CRT stripes in LCD modes. Be scale-aware: preserve sharp readability at 1× or narrow fractional scales (where a full grid could alias or create moiré) and keep pixel cells aligned when resized/full-screen/portrait-rotated.
3. **Temporal LCD persistence:** Use a bounded previous-frame/history texture or lightweight ping-pong buffers to blend successive **emulated** frames. Specify stable per-emulated-frame decay; do not accumulate blur on each `requestAnimationFrame` draw when no new frame was generated. Implement weak persistence for LCD Light and a somewhat stronger but reasonable response for LCD Authentic. Do **not** fake an extra afterimage when paused or on a static frame.
4. **Model-aware presets:** Mono may have a slightly subdued/tinted reflective-LCD look, Color a softer/lower-contrast early color-LCD treatment and SwanCrystal a clearer, lower-ghosting presentation. Apply these only inside selected LCD modes and only as **tasteful approximations**, never as unverified colorimetry or changes to the core framebuffer. The app already knows the physical console via `machine.model()`; do not infer it from game identity or display mode alone.
5. **Lifecycle and image integrity:** Clear/seed temporal history on successful ROM replacement, Restart, physical console change, switching modes, WebGL restoration, and resuming after hidden/paused state where needed to avoid stale-image trails. A failed ROM load or rejected model switch must not corrupt the display. No ghost of a previous game's image may appear in the next one. Preserve native source resolution, correct alpha handling, aspect ratio, portrait `rotate(-90deg)`, fullscreen sizing, overlay empty state, and all input focus/keyboard/touch behavior.
6. **Performance and resilience:** Keep the effect limited to the screen region and the existing active render loop; no independent 60Hz post-processing loop while paused/hidden/idle. Reuse textures and shader programs; avoid per-frame GPU allocations, unnecessary CPU pixel processing or large intermediate framebuffers. Handle unavailable WebGL2, shader compile/link errors, context loss/restoration and low-end/mobile operation by reporting a concise notice and falling back to a playable Clean display. Clear rendering must remain functional even if shaders fail.

### Controls and preferences

- Put a single labeled **Display effect** selector in the existing **Settings / Help** area, near the console/display guidance, instead of adding a large toolbar or settings page. `Clean`, `LCD Light`, `LCD Authentic`, and `Retro CRT` are the available options.
- Persist the selected mode locally in a versioned browser key, separate from cartridge saves, console EEPROM, RTC and sound preferences. If stored data is invalid or storage is denied, fall back safely; never block play.
- The default for new visitors is **LCD Light** when supported; when unsupported use **Clean** and show that the fallback is active. Existing users must be able to choose Clean and keep that choice across reloads and ROM/model switches. Never silently override their explicit choice.
- Do not introduce a pile of adjustment sliders. Keep effect strengths in simple preset constants, with one short explanation that LCD effects are optional stylization; CRT is a creative extra, not an actual WonderSwan display characteristic.
- Switching presets should immediately redraw the current frame even when paused, without advancing emulator cycles, changing the audio state or requiring Restart. Ensure screen focus and dialog behavior remain intuitive.

### Test and documentation plan

Use already included original CC0 assets (Beacon Trail and existing graphics/display probes), plus small synthetic RGBA test patterns where numerical shader tests are more precise. Do not add or require commercial ROMs, proprietary firmware, copied emulator shader code, downloaded textures or copyrighted images.

Prefer a narrowly scoped renderer module (e.g. `web/src/display.ts`) and extend the **existing** production-preview browser tests, reusing their builds/contexts, rather than creating new test tooling or large redundant ROM test suites.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] The player offers the four display modes listed above, with a compact accessible Settings / Help selector. Switching while **running or paused** changes pixels visibly without restarting or advancing the machine, and **Clean** reproduces the existing raw framebuffer accurately.
- [ ] LCD Light / LCD Authentic show genuinely native-pixel-aligned grid/cell detail, subtle softness and distinct levels of persistence. Mono, Color and SwanCrystal have appropriate, modest model-specific treatments. Retro CRT is a separate decorative treatment and never labeled historically authentic.
- [ ] Temporal history advances only on new emulated frames; repeated presentation without new frames causes **no additional ghost decay**. History is cleared/seeded safely across ROM changes, Restart, model changes, mode switches and visibility/pause/resume transitions. Pausing does not black out or distort the last frame.
- [ ] Scale/geometry regression tests cover **224×144 landscape**, **144×224 portrait**, responsive viewport around **375px**, resizing and fullscreen. Grid aligns with the source pixels, rendered aspect and pixel shape remain correct, and touch/keyboard focus and empty-state layering still work.
- [ ] A fresh session defaults to LCD Light when shaders work; user preference persists across reloads and different ROMs/models. Invalid or unavailable localStorage is handled safely. Save data/console EEPROM/RTC/audio preferences are unchanged and separate.
- [ ] WebGL unavailable, shader compile/link failure and `webglcontextlost`/restore paths fail safely to a **working Clean 2D** presentation with clear nonblocking feedback. No shader failure can prevent ROM execution or make the game screen permanently blank.
- [ ] Playwright tests use original CC0 graphics/game fixtures and deterministic patterns to check real shader output differences (pixel grid, preset distinction, previous-frame contribution) rather than only mode labels. Retain meaningful exact-pixel assertions for Clean, and verify fallback, pause, restart and model/orientation cases without redundant full combinations.
- [ ] Existing `npm run build`, `npm run test:browser`, `npm run test:compat` and relevant visual/input regression scripts pass from the production preview. Confirm the Wasm integration still works with the existing build (`npm run build:wasm` if rebuilding is necessary) and note actual test results, failures/skips and browser GPU limitations honestly. No Rust-core or cartridge fixture modifications are required; run additional native checks only if the changed files actually justify them.
- [ ] Update README/Settings help to document modes, per-model aesthetic approximation, Clean fallback and saved preference. Follow current UI/UX and test/CI performance principles; no extraneous UI framework, shader presets, settings page or dependency is added.

## Optional validation

- Compare the looks by eye against photographs of real monochrome WonderSwan, WonderSwan Color and SwanCrystal LCDs **when legally available**, and tune presets without claiming physical color/response fidelity.
- Check Safari/Firefox, physical mobile GPUs and reduced-performance devices. These are useful quality checks but do not block the automated pre-merge acceptance.
- If a minimal CRT variation substantially complicates fallback, rendering, testing or maintenance, record that trade-off explicitly; preserve LCD Light / LCD Authentic / Clean as the required core of this Issue. Do not derail the LCD milestone with elaborate curvature, bloom or scanline simulation.

## Required post-merge verification

1. **Pending:** Confirm the existing `main` GitHub Pages workflow builds and deploys the merge revision successfully, and record the workflow URL. As required by the repository lifecycle, merge and close after all pre-merge criteria pass; do not reopen the Issue just to complete this check.
2. **Pending:** Open the public player and switch Clean/LCD Light/LCD Authentic during an original CC0 game in portrait and landscape; confirm that changing the setting and reloading the page preserve the expected UI, and that audio/input/save controls still work. Note which browsers/GPUs were actually used and any blocked production verification. Track new defects in linked follow-up Issues rather than a review/merge loop.

These are post-merge publication checks, **not** prerequisites to pre-merge approval or closing the completed Issue.
